statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-87910: when tarfile extracts a link on a system that cannot create it, it falls back to extracting the linked member and runs the extraction filter twice; the result of the first call was ignored, so a custom filter that rejected the member by returning None was not honoured. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157265 (3.10 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/c1f106d240c4ffcb3608ed0a20e8aba6c865f6d3), first released in CPython 3.10.22; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/57TBTLL2W6APMZR3A25B2YV7GL3EPTDJ/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-87910, which lists every 3.10 release before 3.10.22 as affected. On the 3.10 branch the first of the two filter calls was added by the gh-151558 fix (https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151558, released in 3.10.21). Checked Lib/tarfile.py in the python-3.10 package of every build of the python-3.10 source published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository by 2026-11-28, 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8, on x86_64 and aarch64 (package sizes checked against the repository index); both architectures ship the same file in each build. 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.20-r9 call the filter once on a link fallback and honour its result (no gh-151558 change); 3.10.20-r10 to 3.10.20-r13 carry a backport of gh-151558 without this fix; 3.10.21-r1 ships the upstream 3.10.21 file, also without it; 3.10.21-r2 ships the upstream 3.10.21 file with this fix backported (the same lines as the 3.10 commit above) and one other backported tarfile change, made before the upstream 3.10.22 release; 3.10.22-r0 to 3.10.22-r4 ship the upstream 3.10.22 file, which has it; 3.10.22-r5 to 3.10.22-r8 add one further backported change to that file and keep it. Builds that predate the gh-151558 change are left on the affected side, matching upstream's affected range. The range ends at 3.10.21-r2. Builds from 3.10.21-r2 on that the CVE record still matches carry the fix.

CVE-2026-87910: when tarfile extracts a link on a system that cannot create it, it falls back to extracting the linked member and runs the extraction filter twice; the result of one call was ignored, so a filter that returned None to skip the member did not stop it from being extracted. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157265 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/764fd0af8d9e19d3684a58d2e58bf770f0605036), first released in CPython 3.12.15; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/57TBTLL2W6APMZR3A25B2YV7GL3EPTDJ/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-87910. Checked makelink_with_filter() in Lib/tarfile.py for the check of the first filter result that the fix adds (if filtered is None: return) in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.12.14-r2 lack the fix; 3.12.14-r2 and every later build have it (3.12.14-r2 carries a backport made before the 3.12.15 release; 3.12.15-r0 and later ship the upstream fix). The range ends at 3.12.14-r2.

The second filter call came from the fix for https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/151558 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/771d12dda5140313db0ac550292987975651bbde, CPython 3.13.15).
